2027-01-30.title: Fourth Saturday of Denha
2027-01-30.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Those who are born of God do not sin
Whoever is from God hears the words of God
2027-01-30.verse: And we know that the Son of God has come and has given us understanding so that we may know him who is true; and we are in him who is true, in his Son Jesus Christ. He is the true God and eternal life.
theo: John ends his first letter by telling us why he wrote it: “so that you may know that you have eternal life.” Christians are not meant to live in anxious guessing. We have “boldness” before God: “if we ask anything according to his will, he hears us.” Then John gives a surprising example of such prayer: praying for a brother or sister who sins. He distinguishes sin that is mortal from sin that is not, the distinction the Church still teaches between mortal and venial sin, and urges us to intercede so that God “will give life” to the one who has fallen. “We know that those who are born of God do not sin”: not that they never stumble, but that they do not make sin their home, because the Son of God protects them. The letter closes with a revelation fit for Denha, “He is the true God and eternal life”, and a final warning: “Little children, keep yourselves from idols.”

In the Gospel Jesus' hearers claim a famous ancestry: “Abraham is our father.” Jesus answers that children resemble their father: “If you were Abraham's children, you would be doing what Abraham did.” Abraham believed and welcomed God's messengers; they are planning to kill the one who tells them the truth. Belonging to God is not a matter of birth certificate but of listening: “Whoever is from God hears the words of God.” The devil, Jesus says, “is a liar and the father of lies.” Every lie we tell, every half-truth we live by, is a small idol. Saturday, the eve of the Lord's Day, is a good day to ask whose children we resemble, to pray for one another's sins, and to prepare for Sunday through the sacrament of Reconciliation.

Confidence in prayer and eternal life.

Mortal and venial sin; the power of intercession.
Doing what Abraham did; hearing God's words.
live: Pray today, by name, for someone you know who has fallen into sin, instead of talking about them.
Examine your conscience tonight and plan to go to confession soon.
2027-01-30.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, true God and eternal life, you have come to give us understanding so that we may know the Father. Keep us from every idol and every lie, hear our prayer for our brothers and sisters who have sinned, and make us true children of Abraham who hear the words of God. Amen.
altar: Before Communion we pray for the forgiveness of sins and receive the One who is true God and eternal life.

2027-01-30.question: Whose child do I resemble in the way I speak and act?

family.explain: Jesus said that if God is our Father, we will love Jesus and listen to his words. Children often look like their parents. God's children look like Jesus when they listen to him and tell the truth.
family.intention: We pray for anyone in our family or parish who has turned away from God.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there a small lie we need to say sorry for today?”

illus: In a parish in Ernakulam a prayer group kept a simple rule: whenever someone mentioned another person's fault, the group stopped and prayed for that person before saying anything more. The leader said: John tells us to pray for a brother who sins, not to discuss him. The gossip stopped, and two people who had left the parish came back that year.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are the true God and eternal life. Keep us in your truth. Amen.
share: If we ask anything according to his will, he hears us (1 John 5:14). Do I pray with confidence?
Little children, keep yourselves from idols (1 John 5:21). What idol do I need to put away?
Whoever is from God hears the words of God (John 8:47). How do I listen to God?
pm.resp: Lord, keep us in your truth.

For those enslaved by lies and deception.
For people searching for the true God.
For our group, that we may pray for one another instead of judging.
pm.close: Father, you have given us your Son, the true God and eternal life. Make us your children in truth and love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, John writes so that you may know that you have eternal life (1 John 5:13). We can pray with boldness, because if we ask anything according to his will, he hears us.

John even tells us what to pray for: a brother or sister who sins. He distinguishes mortal sin from sin that is not mortal, as the Church still does, and promises that God will give life to the one for whom we pray. Instead of judging, we intercede.
In the Gospel Jesus tells those who boast of Abraham: if you were Abraham's children, you would be doing what Abraham did (John 8:39). And: whoever is from God hears the words of God (John 8:47).
Tomorrow is the Lord's Day. Today let us keep ourselves from idols and from lies, pray for one another, and prepare our hearts through confession. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says God's children listen to God and tell the truth. Today, let us pray for someone who has done wrong, and say sorry for our own mistakes.

intro: Theme: “Whoever is from God hears the words of God.”
Confident prayer, intercession for sinners, and the true children of Abraham.

q: The LORD is near to all who call on him, to all who call on him in truth.
And this is the boldness we have in him, that if we ask anything according to his will, he hears us.
points.apply: Pray today with confidence for one need, adding: your will be done.

q: And he believed the LORD; and the LORD reckoned it to him as righteousness.

q: Hear, O Israel: The LORD is our God, the LORD alone.
Whoever is from God hears the words of God. The reason you do not hear them is that you are not from God.”

concl: We know the true God, and we can pray with confidence.
God's children listen to his words and pray for one another.
